title: Man calls out mother for seeking MOE financial aid after $1,000 BTS ticket splurge, Singapore News

 singapore Man calls out mother for seeking MOE financial aid after $1,000 BTS ticket splurge
 A Singapore mother's $1,000 splurge on BTS concert tickets has sparked online debate over her financial priorities after she complained about failing to get school financial aid. PHOTO: Screengrab/Threads PUBLISHED ON November 20, 2026 7:00 AM BY Asyiqin Nadzri A netizen has called out a mother for seeking financial assistance for her children's schooling after she shared that she had spent $1,000 on BTS concert tickets, sparking debate online over financial priorities and the use of government aid.
 In a Threads post on Tuesday (Nov 18), the man shared a screenshot of his response to the mother's post, in which she expressed frustration over her unsuccessful application for the Ministry of Education's (MOE) Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS).
 The mother had written that her FAS application was unsuccessful and that she had emailed the school to enquire about school-based financial assistance, adding that she had yet to receive a reply.
 In response, the man questioned her financial priorities, pointing out that she had previously shared that she spent $1,000 on BTS concert tickets.
 "Why do you abuse our system?," he wrote.
 In his own Threads post, he said: "I really really hate it. You got money to pay for BTS tickets, but still asking for financial assistance scheme. There are others who need it more than you."
 Netizens divided over mother's spending
 The post drew mixed reactions, with some agreeing that the mother's spending raised questions about her financial priorities.
 One netizen questioned how a parent could justify spending $1,000 on concert tickets while struggling to afford their children's school expenses.
 "If you're sympathising the parents who got called out for going to the BTS concert instead of providing for their child...then yes im judging you harshly," the commenter wrote.
 They added that schoolbooks cost less than $150 per child annually and described the mother's spending as "bad financial planning".
 Another argued that the issue was not necessarily whether the mother was exploiting the system, but that her posts could come across as "tone-deaf".
 However, others felt that the mother's eligibility should be assessed based on official criteria rather than her personal spending habits.
 One netizen pointed out that FAS applications are assessed based on household income, adding that an application should be considered regardless of how wealthy an applicant might appear.
 "If someone is entitled for it despite 'looking rich' so be it," the netizen wrote.
 Others also suggested that the mother could have saved up for the concert tickets or set aside money for a personal treat.
 Some netizens who had helped families in need also shared their own experiences.
 One user recalled sponsoring the schoolbooks and uniforms of a family with four children, only to see the mother post about receiving a YSL perfume and a Michael Kors bag from her husband the following day.
 MOE's FAS eligibility is based on household income
 According to MOE, students may qualify for FAS if their family's monthly gross household income (GHI) does not exceed $4,000, or their monthly per capita income (PCI) does not exceed $1,000.
 The scheme provides financial support to eligible students to help defray schooling expenses.
 For primary school students, the scheme covers 100 per cent of miscellaneous fees, as well as free textbooks and school attire.
 Eligible students also receive meal subsidies for seven meals per school week, along with transport subsidies covering 70 per cent of monthly school bus fares or up to $21 per month for those taking public transport.
 AsiaOne has reached out to the netizen and the mother for more information.
